newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Meyer sees trend growth ahead for U.S.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Meyer sees trend growth ahead for U.S.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer predicted Sunday that the U.S. economy would grow at roughly a moderate rate in the months ahead.
"We are now at a point where there are good prospects for growth near trend," he told reporters following an address to to an American Economic Association conference in New Orleans.
He described trend growth as a rate between 2 percent and 2.5 percent, saying it was the "best prospect for the economy going forward."
Meyer, who was named to the Fed Board by President Clinton and assumed his new position last summer, said that at the time the risks in the economy appeared "fairly one-sided."
At that time, the Fed had been worried that low unemployment and an economy that appeared to be growing rather rapidly might raise the prospects for higher inflation.
Now, Meyer said, "The risks appear much more evenly balanced."
He said there seemed to be an equal risk that the economy could grow faster than trend or slower than trend.
However, he said, he did not see any significant excesses that could derail the economic expansion.
He also said he did not see "pockets of strength" that could produce growth significantly above trend.
